pages.title: Welcome
pages.subtitle: Projects are rarely lost at the planning stage

blocks.heading: Where projects actually fail
paragraphs: A charter gets written, a scope gets agreed, a Gantt chart gets built, and then the project is run out of an inbox for four months. It does not fail because the plan was wrong. It fails because nobody owned the deliverable, the week had no shape, and nothing was ever formally closed.

blocks.heading: So this planner is weighted to the middle and the end
items: A responsibility matrix, because a task list with owners is not the same as accountability
A weekly and daily cadence, so the plan meets an actual calendar
Time blocking, because project work loses every contest with reactive work
A closure checklist, because unclosed projects leak cost for months
A final review that separates what happened from what everyone remembers

blocks.heading: The definition pages are deliberately brief
paragraphs: Overview, charter, scope, objectives, success criteria and the work breakdown get one page each. They are here so the project has a spine, not to be a second planning exercise. The weight of this planner sits after the kick-off meeting.

blocks.heading: One planner, one project
paragraphs: Filled completely for a single project rather than sampled across five. If you run several, duplicate the file per project.

pages.title: Instructions
pages.subtitle: Set the spine in an hour, then run the week

blocks.heading: Choose your size
paragraphs: Four sizes are included and all four contain identical pages. A4 and US Letter suit the desk and the wall. A5 and Half Letter suit a tablet and a site visit, and print two-up on a full sheet.

blocks.heading: Set the spine
items: Overview, charter and scope — one page each, thirty minutes total
Objectives and success criteria — how anyone will know this worked
Stakeholder register and team directory
Fill the RACI before the first task is assigned
Break the work down and set the milestones

blocks.heading: Every week
items: Weekly Project Planner — what this week must produce, per day
Time Blocking — book the project work before the calendar fills
Update the task planner, risk register and issue log
Progress Tracker — one line, honestly

blocks.heading: Every day
items: Daily Task Planner — three project tasks, in the blocks you booked
Log anything raised straight into the issue or change log

blocks.heading: At the end
items: Work the Project Closure Checklist line by line
Run the Final Project Review while people still remember
File the lessons somewhere the next project will actually find them
